subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw pursue this Gateway control-plane and per-agent runtime split as a core architecture track, and what first supported milestone should define the protocol, trust model, and lifecycle boundary?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the next step requires choosing public protocol, config, security, lifecycle, deployment, and migration contracts that automation cannot safely decide.

options.title: Approve Phased Runtime Split
options.body: Keep #42026 canonical and sponsor a local-split milestone that defines a clone-safe runtime protocol, callback bridge, trust model, session ownership, and embedded-mode compatibility before container or Kubernetes runners.

options.title: Narrow To Execution Placement
options.body: Treat #82017 and #84758 as the current implementation scope while deferring the broader Gateway/control-plane split until the placement contract is reviewed.

options.title: Defer Core Architecture Change
options.body: Keep supporting multi-gateway and operator workarounds without committing to a distributed runtime boundary now.

recommendation.title: Approve Phased Runtime Split
recommendation.body: Keep #42026 canonical and sponsor a local-split milestone that defines a clone-safe runtime protocol, callback bridge, trust model, session ownership, and embedded-mode compatibility before container or Kubernetes runners.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest related architecture history through the worker-runtime experiment and current-runtime review context.
